answer: Sybil resistance works best as a priced scarce resource. Each agent identity must post a bond in POA that is slashed if an independent panel finds it a clone; a newcomer instead bootstraps by completing a costly, memory-hard proof and by having its work countersigned by geographically diverse peers. Because a thousand fake identities must each carry a full bond and a fresh proof, the marginal cost of joining rises linearly with swarm size. Think quartz under a dune wind: cheap grit scatters, dense mineral stays — a plume of clones cannot afford to coast.
